rules.title: Validity rules
rules.subtitle: Rules check every field minute by minute and raise suspect stretches. A suspect changes nothing: the figures only follow once an Admin confirms it in the review queue. A confirmed detection on a mandatory field makes the component unavailable for that time; on an optional field it marks the field only.

typeHint.stuck: The same value for this many minutes or more is suspect. A missing minute ends the run.
typeHint.spike: A change larger than this between consecutive valid minutes is suspect. A missing minute is never compared.

definitions.title: How the figures are calculated
definitions.subtitle: The definitions behind every availability figure in SIMOLA: the same for the dashboards, the site pages, the exports and the monthly report.
definitions.version: Definitions version {v} · in force from {date} · written down in {source}
definitions.versionNote: The monthly report and the exports carry this version. A change to a formula gets a new version; a change to the mandatory fields does not (it is a setting, recorded in the audit log).

counting.title: How minutes are counted
items: Everything is counted in whole minutes, in UTC. A minute stands for its 60 seconds: 10:42 means 10:42:00 to 10:42:59.
A period runs from its start up to, but not including, its end. A 30-day month has exactly 43,200 minutes.
For a period still running, counting stops {grace} minutes before now, because the newest minutes may still be arriving.
These are the expected minutes. Minutes before the data coverage start ({coverage}) are not expected, and neither are a sensor's minutes outside its in-service period.
Each minute has one merged record: CDP1's, or CDP2's when CDP1 has none or every field of CDP1's is missing.
When no minute is expected, a figure shows “—”, never 0 % or 100 %.

sla.name: SLA (system availability)
sla.what: The share of minutes in which at least one CDP produced data. A minute is lost only when both CDPs produced none.
sla.formula: minutes with data from any CDP ÷ expected minutes × 100

uptime.name: CDP uptime
uptime.what: The share of minutes in which one CDP's 1-minute file has a record for that minute. A record whose fields are all missing still counts.
uptime.formula: minutes with a record in this CDP's file ÷ expected minutes × 100

reach.name: Network reachability
reach.what: The share of probed minutes in which the CDP answered a network probe. For information only: it is not part of SLA or OLA.
reach.formula: minutes with an answer ÷ minutes with a probe × 100
reach.note: Always shown with its probe coverage: the share of minutes that had a probe at all.

component.name: Sensor availability
component.what: The share of minutes in which the merged record has a value in every mandatory field of the sensor, and no manual flag or confirmed detection covers the minute.

dcp.name: DCP availability
dcp.what: A DCP minute is valid when the merged record exists and at least one field of another sensor at the site has a value.
dcp.note: Flags and detections never change the DCP.

site.name: Site availability
site.what: The share of all the site's sensor-minutes, DCP included, that were valid.

ola.name: OLA
ola.what: The average of the sites' availabilities: Runway 04, Runway Middle and Runway 22 weigh the same.
ola.formula: sum of the site availabilities ÷ number of sites

pooled.name: All components
pooled.what: All sensor-minutes of every site together, so a site with more sensors weighs more than in OLA.
pooled.formula: valid sensor-minutes of all sites ÷ (all sensors × expected minutes) × 100

mandatory.title: Mandatory fields now
mandatory.intro: A sensor counts as available in a minute only when every one of its mandatory fields has a value. These are the mandatory fields today. An Admin can change them; the figures are then worked out again and the change is recorded in the audit log.
mandatory.dcp: The merged record and any field of another sensor at the site

changes.title: What else changes a figure
items: Manual flags: an Admin marks a sensor's minutes as not valid, with a reason (sensor fault, maintenance, calibration, environmental, other). A flag costs only minutes that would otherwise be valid.

Confirmed detections: a validity rule (out of range, stuck value or spike) found a stretch of doubtful values in a mandatory field, and an Admin confirmed it. Suspects waiting for review change nothing.
In-service periods: minutes when a sensor was not yet installed, or removed, are not expected.
Reading the CDP files again (a reprocess) brings in data that arrived late or was corrected.
Every such change is recorded in the audit log, and the figures follow within minutes.
changes.link: Data quality: what flags and detections cost each sensor

rounding.title: Rounding and colours
items: Figures are worked out from whole minute counts and shown with two decimals, rounded half up. They are never capped: more than 100 % cannot happen.
The valid and expected minutes are shown with every figure.

Colours: {good} % or more is good, {warning} % or more is a warning, and below that is bad. The darkest colour means no minute was lost, so a figure that rounds to 100.00 % but lost a minute is shown one step lighter.
